newsitem.title: USA: U.S. statistical agency to review Boskin advice.
newsitem.headline: U.S. statistical agency to review Boskin advice.

text.p: The agency that issues the monthly Consumer Price Index on Wednesday said it will review an independent panel's suggestions for changing the index, and will provide some specific responses in a few weeks.

"We will be looking seriously at all of the report's recommendations over the coming weeks and months, and expect to have prepared some more complete response to these recommendations within the next few weeks," Katharine Abraham, commissioner for the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, said in a statement.
A congressionally appointed commission led by Stanford University professor Michael Boskin earlier Wednesday issued a report concluding the CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year.
The panel recommended a series of actions by Congress and the Clinton administration but also made several technical suggestions to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Abraham said her agency has at least one difference of opinion with the Boskin group. Specifically, the BLS has reservations about adopting so-called geometric mean formula for calculating the index as the panel advised.
Starting early next year, the BLS will put out an experimental index using the geometric mean but Abraham said her agency is still studying whether officially adopting that formula would make sense.
"We do not believe that adequate evidence for reaching that conclusion now exists," she said. "This is, however, something that BLS is actively investigating."
